result.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
result.summary: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EffectWAM 世界-动作模型：以「Effect」表示相对当前观测锚点的视觉变化，配合相机位姿编码与动作接地训练，用 flow matching 共享生成专家同时预测视觉变化和可执行动作块，使控制器无需等待视频合成即可动作。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用动作接地监督让视觉表示保留末端位姿变化、并以 EMA 编码器提供目标，可供核查 LVR 中「latent 是否承载任务必要视觉变化」及动作预测与视觉生成的解耦；但属机器人策略工作，与 VLM 推理状态生成关系需进一步判断。
